title: Alert Priority Decay — experiment log and oncall runbook
content:
Context:
We continue to get repeated low-impact pages at 03:00–06:00 UTC from the inference-gateway path errors. Historically these are transient (retries clear them) but still wake up oncall and contribute to SRE burnout and noisy SLO burn alerts. This doc captures a small-run experiment: introduce a time-based priority-decay layer for non-critical alerts so repeated flapping reduces page urgency and routes to a lower-cost channel while keeping visibility for eventual escalation.

Goals / success criteria (30d experiment):
- Reduce P1/P2 page volume from the gateway alert group by >= 35% during trial window (measured by PagerDuty incidents tagged gateway-experiment).
- No increase in customer-visible errors (latency errors, 5xxs) per product SLOs beyond historical variance (+5% drift threshold).
- Maintain ability to surface a sustained regression: if a decayed alert persists > 15m at steady-state rate, it escalates to full priority.

Hypothesis:
- Many pages are identical flakes that repeat within a short time window (several retries). If we demote repeated occurrences of the same fingerprint within a decay window, we preserve signal for new regressions while removing noisy duplicates.

Experiment design (implementation sketch):
1) Alert fingerprinting: for each alert rule, compute a short fingerprint (alert name + service + route + first 3 chars of error message + host-pool tag). Store in a lightweight Redis TTL=900s.
2) First occurrence => route as normal (P1/P2 depending on rule).
3) If the same fingerprint reoccurs within the TTL: apply "priority decay" policy: map P1->P2, P2->P3, P3->log-only. Create a transformed incident in PagerDuty with suffix "-decayed" and tag "decay-experiment".
4) Escalation clause: if decayed incident count for that fingerprint exceeds 5 within 15 minutes OR cumulative error rate for that route exceeds 2x baseline in last 5 minutes, promote back to original priority and escalate to oncall.
5) Observability: emit telemetry: alert.fingerprint, alert.original_priority, alert.current_priority, decay_count, time_since_first, route_error_rate.

Prometheus queries (examples to track):
- Baseline rate by route: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (route)
- Error rate (5xx): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)
- Decayed alerts count: sum(increase(alerts_total{tag="decay-experiment",status="firing"}[1h]))
- Escalation triggers: sum(increase(alert_escalations_total{experiment="priority-decay"}[1h]))

Runbook (oncall steps if you receive a decayed incident):
1) Check the PagerDuty incident title. If it ends with "-decayed" and has tag "decay-experiment" treat as lower urgency but do a sanity check: open the error dashboard for the route referenced in the incident.
2) Run the quick checks:
   - Is the route 5xx rate > baseline by >2x? (use the PromQL above)
   - Are latency percentiles (p95) > SLO threshold?
   - Are there corresponding cluster-level infra alerts (node OOM, GPU saturation)?
3) If the answers are all negative and the decayed_count < 5, file a short note on the incident and mark "acknowledge (do not escalate)". If any of the escalation clauses are met, press "promote to original priority" (internal runbook button) which triggers full-page routing and paging policy.
4) Document any temporary mitigations used (eg: toggle feature flag, increase replica count), and attach graphs to the PagerDuty incident for post-run analysis.

Metrics to observe during experiment:
- PagerDuty incidents per alert group per hour (pre/post comparison).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for decayed incidents vs regular.
- Rate of false negatives: cases where a decayed incident masked a real regression (manual classification after the fact).
- SLO burn: error budget spend for the last 14d and during experiment window.

Safety & rollback plan:
- Canary: enable in 2 clusters (us-east-1 and eu-west-1) for a rolling 72h window. Observe for 24h. If customer-facing errors exceed threshold or a manual escalation occurs that was incorrectly decayed, immediately disable (feature flag) and revert routing.
- Kill switch: PagerDuty mapping is behind a feature flag + routing config; engineering can flip back in <5 minutes.

Data collection / labeling for follow-up:
- Tag decayed incidents in PD with label "auto-decayed" and add a short classification checklist for owners to mark: accidental-suppression | acceptable-suppression | missed-regression. We will sample 50 incidents/week for manual review.

Open questions / risks:
- Fingerprinting collision risk: if fingerprint is too coarse we may conflate separate failures. Mitigate by including host-pool and truncated error hash; consider switching to vector similarity later.
- Volume dynamics: decay TTL tuning will require balancing — too long and we hide separate incidents; too short and we don't reduce noise. Start TTL=900s (15m).
- Alert owner workflows: product/domain owners might not like reduced priority on their rules. We need a communications plan (email + slack thread to affected owners and SLO owners prior to rollout).

Initial results (first 72h canary, us-east-1 + eu-west-1):
- PagerDuty incidents for gateway group down 42% (hourly median), decayed incidents accounted for ~60% of previous pages.
- No sustained increase in customer SLO error budget spend; short bursts observed but rolled back under escalation clauses.
- Two manual escalations where PD decayed incidents masked a new regression; both had identical fingerprint but different upstream root cause (one was a client malformed payload spike). We adjusted fingerprint to include first 7 chars of payload-type header for that route.

Follow-ups planned:
- Expand TTL experiment matrix: try 5m, 10m, 15m, 30m in A/B groups.
- Work with product teams to annotate alert rules with recommended decay sensitivity (low/med/high).
- Add an automated weekly digest of "decayed but reviewed" incidents for owners.
- Propose a new SLO-linked policy: if an alert is tied to an SLO with error budget <20%, decay is disabled for that alert (preserve strictness when budget low).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; implementation PR is open under linked_artifacts. Please leave comments in the confluence draft or the PR for technical changes. We should schedule a 30m sync with affected product owners to walk through the early results before broad rollout.

Appendix: example pseudo-rule (implementation-friendly)
- name: gateway-5xx-high
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="gateway",status=~"5.."}[2m])) by (route) > 0.05
  for: 1m
  labels: {severity: "P1"}
  on_fire: create_alert(fingerprint=sha1(name + route + substr(err,0,7) + host_pool))
  routing: if fingerprint_seen_recently && decay_count < 5 => map_priority(decay_map) else normal_route

End.
